fatal_errors: The specific lightweight MgAlTiVFeCo BCC alloy is replaced by the overly broad category of high-entropy alloys.
The decisive intervention—spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C—is omitted.
The proposed mechanism does not identify densification, oxide barrier-phase precipitation, passive-film formation, chloride blocking, or diffusion-controlled parabolic oxidation.
The boundary of applications above 800 °C is not the target processing window of 800–1000 °C and omits magnesium volatilization above 1000 °C.
The lightweight claim is not supported by the cited evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis captures only the broad material class and generic expectations of high hardness, corrosion resistance, and thermal stability. It does not reconstruct the MgAlTiVFeCo composition, SPS processing, optimal 1000 °C condition, oxide barrier phases, or the reported density, hardness, oxidation, and electrochemical results. The evidence supports general HEA attributes but not this alloy or its lightweight character; E1 also cautions that some HEAs decompose at elevated temperature. The proposed experiment is broadly falsifiable, but comparison against traditional alloys cannot distinguish the target temperature-dependent SPS mechanism.
